# `prefer-arena`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a scope with at least three allocations from one allocator and a
matching release for each.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

That lifetime already behaves like an arena; making it structural removes
repetitive cleanup and leak opportunities.

## When it fires

Only same-scope allocation and `defer` release shapes are counted: an
`errdefer` release keeps the allocation alive on success, which an arena would
not. A function passed to `checkAllAllocationFailures` is exempt, since it
exists to fail and release each allocation in turn, and so are test blocks,
private functions only tests reach, and allocators declared from
`std.testing.allocator` or a failing allocator: a leak-checking test releases
each allocation on purpose, and one arena would hide a leak. No rewrite is
offered because changing ownership strategy is a design decision.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn work(gpa: std.mem.Allocator) !void {
    const a = try gpa.alloc(u8, 16);
    defer gpa.free(a);
    const b = try gpa.alloc(u8, 32);
    defer gpa.free(b);
    const c = try gpa.alloc(u8, 64);
    defer gpa.free(c);
}
```
